title: Set up custom domain
summary: Register domain, configure DNS, set up SSL, point to hosting.

parts.title: Search domain availability
parts.guidance: Search the exact proposed names and extensions at the registrar that would handle registration. Compare initial and renewal prices, premium or resale listings, and any extension restrictions. Keep the spelling and check time with the shortlist because availability can change. Flag apparent naming conflicts for the brand-clearance work.

parts.title: Register domain
parts.guidance: Register the exact domain and term authorized by the purchaser, checking spelling, registrant details, renewal settings and optional extras at checkout. Use the company-controlled account and complete its contact-verification steps. After payment, confirm the domain appears under the intended registrant with the expected expiration and renewal arrangement. Put renewal notices and account recovery with maintained company contacts, and retain the registration receipt privately.

verify.how: An RDAP/WHOIS lookup shows the domain registered to you (or your registrar's privacy proxy) with the expected expiry date.

parts.title: Transfer DNS to Cloudflare
parts.guidance: Export the current zone before moving authoritative DNS to Cloudflare. Compare imported records against the export, especially mail and verification records, and review the provider's instructions for existing DNSSEC and proxy settings. Under the domain owner's change authorization, replace nameservers with the values assigned to this zone. Check authoritative answers and actual website and mail behavior after the switch. Use the exported zone to diagnose and restore missing records.

references.title: Set up a primary DNS zone

parts.title: Configure DNS records
parts.guidance: Compare the host's required DNS values with records already present at each name. Preserve unrelated mail, verification and subdomain records, and apply the smallest authorized change set. Query authoritative DNS first, then a public resolver and the affected service. Differences can be investigated against the old values and TTLs. Keep the before-and-after zone entries so a bad change can be reversed without reconstructing them from memory.

references.title: Set up a primary DNS zone

parts.title: Add domain to Vercel
parts.guidance: Attach the hostname to the intended hosting project within the domain and hosting owners' authorized scope. On Vercel, use the validation status and DNS values shown for that specific domain. Set the intended canonical hostname and redirects, then open each customer-facing hostname to verify the project and deployment it serves. Check HTTPS separately: adding the domain starts certificate work, but successful DNS validation is still needed.

parts.title: Verify SSL
parts.guidance: Open the site over HTTPS on every supported hostname, including redirect sources. Inspect certificate names and validity, then exercise pages and API calls for certificate or mixed-content failures. On Vercel, investigate pending issuance against domain validation, DNS/proxy settings and certificate-authority restrictions. Make traffic-affecting corrections within the domain owner's change scope. Confirm renewal-failure notices reach someone who can repair the configuration.

metadata.supportReason: Namecheap and Cloudflare APIs fully support domain/DNS operations. SSL auto-provisioned.
